doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Learning flute and the Illinois doctorate
summary: A stepmother's gift of a flute at 14-15, classical lessons in Indianapolis, and the experience of doctoral study at Illinois as the oldest student.

bands.name: University of Illinois Latin Jazz band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Oh yeah, you know it’s interesting that you bring the albums up, because the first album I heard was “Afro Classics” and this is, I think I was 14, 15 years old. My stepmother gave me a flute, I went into a closet and was hyperventilating trying to get a sound out of that thing. And after that I said well — and I looked at his life, because he studied at Juilliard. So I said you really want to play the instrument well. Because once you do that then you can go and learn the language of jazz. So I started to take classical flute lessons and I did that in [inaudible] in Indianapolis I studied with a guy named Albert Saurini who used to be principal at Indianapolis, and then I finally met Karen Moratz who is the present principal now, and I got my master’s with her. And then I wanted to get a doctorate but IU didn’t have a doctorate in jazz performance. So I went to the University of Illinois and they let me in, so I was playing trumpet parts and stuff with the Latin Jazz band for three years and had to transpose a lot of stuff.

Oh yeah so I had to do that a while. But it was probably the best experience of my life, Monk. It’s interesting. I would sit — we had a thing called a jazz forum at 11:00 on a Friday afternoon. Well I’m the oldest guy in the school, I was probably older than the teachers when I went there. This was about ten years ago. So I’m sitting there and I had to pinch myself. I said I’m sitting here listening and playing music, playing jazz, and guys my age either hate their job and want to get out or try and retire. So it was a great experience. And my family was a little bit different too then because my kids had all grown up, my wife was actually working for the Army in Saudi Arabia. So Illinois was about 125 miles from home so I would get — I got a little flea bag apartment, it really was a flea bag. But I’d drive back home on the weekends to make sure the house was okay. And then I went to fly over to see her several times in the meantime. So my life has been kind of up and, kind of interesting.
